questions.question: Explain what a river's source and mouth are, and give three places where a river can begin.
questions.expected_answer: The source is where a river begins, and the mouth is where it ends. A river can begin at a spring, in a wetland, where snow melts, or where many small streams join high in the mountains.

questions.question: Why do rivers always flow from high areas to low areas? Describe how a river changes from its source to its mouth.
questions.expected_answer: Rivers flow downhill because gravity pulls water down. Near the source, in the upper course, a river is narrow and fast in a steep V-shaped valley. In the middle course, it becomes wider and deeper and makes bends. In the lower course, it is wide and slow, crossing flat land in meanders.

questions.question: Explain the directions in which rivers flow in South Africa, with an example.
questions.expected_answer: Rivers that begin east of the escarpment have a short, steep journey and flow east to the Indian Ocean, such as the Thukela. Rivers on the plateau mostly flow west across the gently sloping interior, join the Gariep, and reach the Atlantic Ocean at Alexander Bay. Some northern rivers flow into the Limpopo, which reaches the Indian Ocean through Mozambique.
